html:
SMTO-GML-0051 — Gmail refused to sign in with your saved Gmail account

GUID: c8823e3e-7743-52b0-bba5-022541330995
Slug: gmail-app-password-authentication
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail_imap

What happened

  • Gmail refused to sign in to the Gmail account saved for this task, so SMTO couldn't open your mailbox. Most often the app password no longer works, but Gmail didn't say exactly why.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open More options › Parameter Store, select your Gmail account, open the Value tab and select Reveal & edit value. Check that email is the full Gmail address. Gmail only accepts an app password together with the exact address it was created for.
  2. Create a new app password in your Google Account (2-Step Verification must be on), paste it as the app_password value, and select Save. App passwords stop working if they are removed, or when the Google Account password is changed.
  3. If the Gmail address belongs to a work or school, ask its Google administrator whether app passwords are allowed for your account. If app passwords are turned off by the administrator, Gmail rejects every app password.
  4. Ask SMTO to test the Gmail connection for this account. If your request was sending or changing mail, check Sent and Drafts in Gmail before asking for it again. The test signs in without touching mail, and checking first avoids sending the same email twice.

What success looks like

  • The Gmail connection test succeeds, and your request finishes with a result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Never paste the app password into a conversation, and don't switch to a different account or sign-in method to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The IMAP sign-in to imap.gmail.com for the selected gmail_app_password_account failed with a pre-authentication IMAP4.error (error_kind gmail_app_password_rejected), so no mailbox session was opened; provider text is omitted, so a greeting rejection looks the same.

What this means

  • The IMAP server rejected authentication for the selected saved account. Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.

Why this can happen

  • Producer condition: The IMAP server rejected authentication for the selected saved account.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact account revision, Gateway route and failing substep with the retained receipt.

How to fix it

  • Verify the email and app_password fields of the selected gmail_app_password_account parameter, confirm Google 2-Step Verification is on and the account or Workspace policy allows app passwords, then run gmail.test_connection. The Gateway omits provider text, so the same pre-authentication IMAP4.error also covers greeting rejections; confirm with the test before replacing the credential.
  • Check the saved email address and Google app password. Confirm that 2-Step Verification and the account policy permit app passwords, then run Gmail test_connection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Preserve confirmed work and establish the current mailbox state before any repeated write.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation completes with a matching receipt, or the remaining uncertain action is inspected in Gmail without duplicate mail.

What not to do

  • Do not switch accounts or authentication methods after failure, or automatically replay uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.
  • App-password setup: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
